email.body1:
Gabriela, saw Incode launched Agentic Identity and deepened the Interac partnership in Canada.

Opening a new category usually means more in-market accounts in play than the team can cover before reps and enablement ramp, and that is where deals stall. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Incode off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Gabriela, quick follow-up for Incode.

Launching Agentic Identity adds a whole new buyer set, and pipeline expectations usually outrun what headcount can absorb. Most teams cannot actually say how many meetings they need to seed the new category, so the gap shows up late.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Incode needs to cover that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Gabriela, last bit of proof for Incode.

Memgraph had more accounts in play than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Incode's reply rate likely compares to other category-defining startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
